title: Gochujang Pork Tenderloin
subtitle: Sheet-pan batch. 4 servings. 12 min prep, 25 min roast.

ingredients.thai_market_tip: Tops/Makro carry whole tenderloins in vac-pack. Cheapest lean protein per gram in the supermarket. Trim the silver-skin or it'll be chewy.
Chung Jung One red tub, Korean aisle.

ingredients.note: Goes in the glaze — total fat for 4 servings, well within oil cap.

substitutions.note: Cook 18 min instead of 25. Brine 15 min first or it'll dry.
Loses some glaze shine, drops 50 kcal across the batch.

steps.text: Whisk gochujang, soy, rice vinegar, honey, sesame oil, garlic, ginger. Reserve 1/3 for serving — the other 2/3 is the cooking glaze.
Brush cooking glaze all over tenderloins. Lay on one half of a sheet pan, lined with parchment.
Toss vegetables with 1 tsp neutral oil, salt. Spread on the other half of the sheet pan.
Roast 22–25 min until internal temp is 63°C / 145°F at the thickest part. Vegetables should char at the edges.
Rest tenderloins 5 min, then slice into 1.5cm medallions.
Portion into 4 containers: 1/4 of pork, 1/4 of vegetables, drizzle of reserved glaze, sesame + spring onion. Keeps 4 days fridge.

serves_with.note: 1 pack adds ~200 kcal / 43g carbs. Best with the leftover glaze drizzled over.

notes: Pork tenderloin is the most underrated protein in the Thai supermarket — cheap, lean, big macros, and the gochujang glaze hides any blandness. 63°C internal is the sweet spot (juicy, safe). Rest is non-negotiable; cut early and you bleed all the juice. Reserve a third of the glaze raw — it stays brighter than the roasted version.
